answer_text:
Here are some of the best places to find the latest stock market news:

---

### 📰 Top Sources for Stock Market News

1. **[CNBC](https://www.cnbc.com)** – One of the most popular financial news outlets. Stocks recently closed at record highs with tech leading the way. The Nasdaq gained 8% in May. CNBC offers live updates, video, and expert analysis.

2. **[Yahoo Finance](https://finance.yahoo.com/topic/stock-market-news/)** – A comprehensive hub for market data and news. The May nonfarm payrolls report and Broadcom earnings are currently in focus for investors.

3. **[CNN Markets](https://www.cnn.com/markets)** – CNN offers up-to-date stock market data coverage, including the latest updates on US markets, world markets, stock quotes, crypto, commodities, and currencies.

4. **[Nasdaq.com](https://www.nasdaq.com)** – Get the latest stock market news, stock information & quotes, data analysis reports, as well as a general overview of the market landscape from Nasdaq.

5. **[NYSE.com](https://www.nyse.com/index)** – The official New York Stock Exchange website provides market recaps and insights. For example, the S&P 500 recently ended a week up over 1%, hitting yet another record high and closing in on the next whole number milestone at 7,600.

6. **[Edward Jones – Daily Market Recap](https://www.edwardjones.com/us-en/market-news-insights/stock-market-news/daily-market-recap)** – This site keeps you up to date with the latest developments, trends, and daily insights on the market, offering a comprehensive look at market movements, international updates, economic indicators, and expert analysis.

7. **[Morningstar](https://www.morningstar.com/markets)** – Great for in-depth analysis. For instance, Morningstar covers how the Middle East conflict is exacerbating the task of projecting oil and natural gas prices, plus airline stocks most vulnerable to higher fuel costs.

---

### 💡 Tips for Staying Informed:
- **Set up alerts** on apps like Yahoo Finance or CNBC for real-time notifications.
- **Follow newsletters** from sources like CNBC or Morningstar for daily or weekly summaries.
- **Check economic calendars** for upcoming data releases (like jobs reports or earnings) that can move markets.
